artworks.title: Circe Invidiosa
artworks.description: Waterhouse's tall oil (Art Gallery of South Australia) freezes Ovid's jealousy: Circe pours emerald poison into the bay where Scylla will bathe, turning Glaucus' rejected love into the strait-monster of Messina.

music.title: Scylla et Glaucus
music.description: Leclair's only surviving tragédie en musique — Glaucus, Scylla, and Circe's revenge staged for the Paris Opéra from Ovid's Metamorphoses.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Books 13–14: the fisherman-god loves Scylla, Circe loves him, and poison in the bay makes the dog-girt rock of the strait.

popCulture.title: Glaucus
popCulture.description: The Anthedonian fisherman made sea-god — Scylla's rejected suitor whose name still means the blue-green deep.
